q: 1. How many times has the Civil Service Act - 2049, been amended so far?
explain: The Civil Service Act, 2049 has undergone four significant amendments to date.

q: 2. In which article of the constitution of Nepal, the formation of the Government Civil Service system is included?
explain: Article 285 of the Constitution of Nepal provides for the formation of the Government Civil Service and other government services.

q: 3. According to the Civil Service Act, 2049, 'Permanent post' means, a post of the civil service which is;
options: of which term is not specified
explain: A permanent post is defined as a pensionable post of the Civil Service for which no time limit is fixed.

q: 4. According to the Civil Service Act, 2049 and the Civil Service Rules, 2050, how many groups are there under the Nepal Administrative Service?
explain: Nepal Administrative Service consists of 3 groups: General Administration, Revenue, and Accounts.

q: 5. How many groups are formed under the Nepal Engineering Service as per the Civil Service Rules, 2050?
explain: As per current rules, there are 15 distinct groups under the Nepal Engineering Service (Civil, Electrical, Mechanical, etc.).

q: 6. How many classes are there in non-gazette level of civil service of Nepal?
explain: The non-gazetted level includes 5 classes: First, Second, Third, Fourth, and the unclassified (shreni-bihin) category.

q: 7. Which section of the Civil service Act, 2049 has provisioned about fulfillment of Vacancy in Civil service under the three chapters?
explain: Section 7 of the Civil Service Act, 2049 details the procedures and percentages for filling vacant posts.

q: 8. According to civil service Act - 2049, what percent of allocation has been made for non-gazette first class in the open competition?
explain: For Non-Gazetted First Class (Nayab Subba), 40% of posts are allocated for open competition.

q: 9. What percent of the total vacant post are recruited by open competition in the non-gazette first class level of civil service of Nepal?
explain: Similar to question 25, 40% is the fixed percentage for open recruitment at the Non-Gazetted First Class level.

q: 10. According to Civil Service Act- 2049, what percent of allocation has been made for non-gazette second class in the free competition?
explain: For Non-Gazetted Second Class (Kharidar), 70% of posts are filled through free competition.

q: 11. According to civil service Act - 2049, what percent of allocation has been made for gazette first class in the free competition?
explain: For Gazetted First Class (Sahayak Sachiv/Under Secretary), only 10% are recruited via open competition.

q: 12. How many districts has the Civil Service Act -2049, covered under 'backward area'?
explain: There are 9 districts defined as backward areas (Achham, Kalikot, Jajarkot, Jumla, Dolpa, Bajhang, Bajura, Mugu, and Humla).

q: 13. Which section of the Civil service Act-2049, has provisioned about disqualifications for being candidate under chapter three?
explain: Section 10 of the Act lists the reasons an individual might be disqualified from joining the civil service.

q: 14. The minimum age required for entering into gazette post of government of Nepal is;
explain: To apply for a Gazetted post, the candidate must have attained the age of 21 years.

q: 15. For how long is the probation period for a new permanent employee in Civil Service?
options: 1 year for men and 6 months for women
explain: The probation period is 1 year for male employees and 6 months for female employees.

q: 16. According to Civil Service Act -2049, what is the age limitation for the retirement of a civil servant in Nepal?
explain: Currently, the age of mandatory retirement for civil servants in Nepal is 58 years.

q: 17. Which section provisioned 'professional organization of civil employees'?
explain: Section 53 of the Civil Service Act, 2049 contains provisions relating to professional organizations.

q: 18. Which section has provisioned about the 'Statement of property'?
explain: Section 54 requires civil servants to submit an annual statement of their property/assets.

q: 19. 'No civil employee shall subject any one to torture', which section deals with this?
explain: Section 54 (a) was added to ensure civil servants do not engage in or subject others to torture.

q: 20. Which of the following punishment is not included in the ordinary punishments that may be subjected to the departmental punishments to the employees of Civil Service?
options: Withholding of promotion for two years or withholding of two salary increments
Withholding of two to five salary increments
Removal from service, without being disqualified for government service in the future.
explain: Ordinary punishments include censure and withholding increments/promotions. Removal from service is categorized as a 'Special Punishment' under the Civil Service Act.

q: 21. In which of the following circumstances, a civil employee may be removed from service, without being disqualified for government service in the future if he/she?
options: frequently violates the matters relating to conduct
explain: According to Section 61, repeated indiscipline, political participation, and conduct violations are all grounds for removal without future disqualification.

q: 22. Which of following punishment is subjected to a civil employee, if his/her performance didn't found satisfactory?
options: withholding of promotion for upto two years
withholding of a maximum of two salary increments
explain: Poor performance or failing to meet job responsibilities can result in any of these ordinary departmental punishments.

q: 23. How many types of leave are provided under the Civil Service Act, 2049?
explain: There are 9 types of leave: Casual, Festival, Home, Sick, Maternity/Maternity Care, Study, Extraordinary, Substitution, and Paternity leave.

q: 24. According to Civil Service Rules 2050, there is a provision that employees can get festival leave without increasing it by ------- days throughout the year.
explain: Civil servants are granted 6 days of casual leave and 6 days of festival leave (total 12) per year.

q: 25. What does a suspended employee get during the period of suspension from the regular job, as per to Civil Service Act, 2049?
options: Half of the salary amount and festival allowance
Half of the salary amount and half of the festival allowance
One fourth of the salary amount and festival allowance
explain: During suspension, an employee is only entitled to half of their basic salary to meet subsistence needs.

q: 26. According to Civil Service Rules-2050, how many days civil servant can get sick leave per year?
explain: A civil servant is entitled to 12 days of fully paid sick leave every year.

q: 27. According to Civil Service Rules 2050, In cases where a female civil employee becomes pregnant, how many days of maternity leave is there?
explain: Following the latest amendments to align with labor laws, maternity leave has been extended to 98 days.

q: 28. According to the civil service rules, if the wife of a male civil servant gives birth, how many days of maternity care leave?
explain: A male civil servant is entitled to 15 days of maternity care (paternity) leave to look after his wife and newborn.

q: 29. According to Civil Service Rules 2050, how many days can an employee accumulate the vacation leave he/she has earned?
explain: Home leave can be accumulated up to a maximum of 180 days throughout the service period.

q: 30. How many years of permanent service period should an employee has completed to get study leave?
explain: A civil servant must complete at least 3 years of permanent service to become eligible for study leave.

q: 31. Which of the following leave is not available to an employee of the Civil Service?
explain: 'Visit leave' is not a recognized category of leave under the Nepal Civil Service Rules.

q: 32. Which body recommends the appointment of the heads of constitutional bodies in Nepal?
explain: The Constitutional Council is the specialized body tasked with recommending names for heads and members of constitutional commissions to the President.

q: 33. How many parts were there in 'Nepal Gazette'?
explain: The Nepal Gazette is organized into 6 distinct parts, each categorizing different types of government notices, acts, and rules.
